actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.

Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by voice vote.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 5185.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H5304-5319)
Mr. Schmidt moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill.
Ordered to be Reported by Voice Vote.

dimensions.assessment: Affects federal compilers of the United States Code and legal researchers by correcting obsolete statutory cross-references.
dimensions.evidence: This Act makes technical and conforming changes to the U.S. Code that are related to the enactment of Title 41 (Public Contracts) into positive law.

dimensions.assessment: Effects are strictly administrative and clerical, correcting names, citations, and numbering without altering substantive legal rights or duties.
dimensions.evidence: The purpose of this Act is to make improvements in the enactment of title 41, United States Code, into a positive law title and to improve the Code.

dimensions.assessment: Does not involve federal spending, appropriations, revenue changes, or economic modifications.
Extensive in code-wide breadth due to touching numerous titles, but narrow in legal substance as all changes are purely conforming corrections.
dimensions.evidence: Table of contents sections covering Titles 2 through 52 of the United States Code.

dimensions.assessment: Permanent technical revisions incorporated into the text of the United States Code.

importance_detail.rationale: The bill makes technical, clerical, and conforming corrections across multiple titles of the U.S. Code following the enactment of Title 41 into positive law. It carries negligible substantive policy impact as it updates outdated statutory references without changing underlying laws.
